picks.title: As too much of the industry embrace their own death through genAI, Konami say it's real people that are most important for making good games
picks.rationale: Konami goes on record that people, not AI efficiency gains, drive innovative games. It is a new major-publisher position that joins the Sega and Capcom stances already in the section.
picks.excerpt: "Even if AI use does lead to improvements in production efficiency I believe that the most important factors in producing... innovative video games are people."

picks.title: Tech founder criticized for vibe coding game about shooting 'zombies' in San Francisco's poorest neighborhood
picks.rationale: A vibe-coded web game was pulled after city residents and leaders denounced it. This is a concrete takedown that shows the reputational risk when fast AI prototyping meets real places and people.
picks.excerpt: City residents and leaders denounced the free web game, which was taken down.

picks.title: Accused of using AI in World of Warcraft Forever videos, Blizzard employee says "hell nah, we have real team members"
picks.rationale: Blizzard states it uses no AI on any of its social content, a clear disclosure line from a major studio at a time when players are quick to call out AI art.
picks.excerpt: "We don't use AI on ANY social content we make"

picks.title: Google Play launches discoverability tool Game Finder using "gamer DNA"
picks.rationale: A new Google Play feature uses Google AI to build a "gamer DNA" profile from play habits and recommend games by genre and mechanic. It changes how mobile games get found, and players can filter out titles that push in-app purchases.
picks.excerpt: Google Play's Game Finder uses Google AI to build a "gamer DNA" profile from play habits, then recommends games by genre and mechanic. Players can also filter out titles that push in-app purchases.

picks.title: Wooga's Holger Wurst on designing June's Journey: Player research, AI and the UX rule you can't break
picks.rationale: The UI/UX lead on a $1B live game, who runs a team of 11, explains where AI helps and where it falls short in live-game UX, and why player research comes first. It is directly useful craft guidance for game designers.
picks.excerpt: Wooga's UI/UX lead on the $1B hidden-object game June's Journey, who runs 11 designers, animators and researchers, talks through AI's possibilities and limits for live-game UX and why player research still comes first.
